newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products trade quietly, with prices steady.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products trade quietly, with prices steady.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Friday in very quiet business, traders said.
Gas oil presented a confused picture as bullish sentiment sparked by higher-than-expected Indian diesel tender awards and a couple of high price buys by a major petered out.
News that state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) had awarded some 855,000 tonnes worth of diesel tenders for July delivery gave the market a temporary boost late on Thursday and early Friday.
But traders said its bullish effects were dissipated later on as players came to terms with the fact that large quantities of Russian material were still overhanging the market.
"The market's still long and much of the Indian material will come out of the Mideast not Mediterranean.
Traders said with freight costs around $25 a tonne the arbitrage window to the East was still note quite open.
Russian material was offered at quotes fob +$1.0 but bids were stuck around the flat to -$1.0 level.
Italian islands prices, meanwhile, were pegged around quotes fob hi flat/+$1.0.
Gasoline was supported by tightness and a cargo was heard done at high fob quotes +$2-3. Traders said there was talk of bringing NWE southwards, but nothing was seen yet.

Fuel oil was seen supported by a dip in supplies of Russian material. Only one cargo of Black Sea was believed loading for sale on the spot market in the early part of next week, with good buying interest still apparent.

Italian refiners were heard still in the market for straight-run material, with future supplies at risk from rumours that Volga river levels were dipping, cutting into the amounts that barges can carry and possibly blocking traffic.
"I think high sulphur prices are fairly static but the outright price may well edge higher if these Russian fears are correct," said one trader.
